themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion in Flatbush
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 22 this week (vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks)—an 826% increase with z-score of 9.27—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or deteriorating enforcement in CD 309.
evidence: 22 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average (826% spike)
Z-score of 9.27 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Highest z-score among all 311 spikes in dataset, signaling acute problem
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and Sanitation about whether this is organized tagging or gang activity
Map complaint hotspots to identify which neighborhoods within Flatbush/PLG are most affected; compare to city's graffiti response times

themes_detail.label: Traffic Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints jumped to 7 last week vs. 1.4 weekly average (409% increase, z-score 3.57), suggesting either new infrastructure disruptions, construction, or illegal parking blocking roads in the district.
evidence: 7 traffic complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (409% increase)
No active ULURP applications or major construction permits suggest spike may be traffic enforcement or event-related
reporting_angles: Cross-check with DOT incident reports and recent street closures; verify if spike correlates with specific intersections or avenues
Interview residents about commute delays; investigate whether illegal parking (1,961 complaints over 90 days) is exacerbating congestion

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber/Lyft) jumped to 3 last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (243% spike, z-score 6.43), indicating possible surge in illegal pickups, unsafe driving, or congestion from TLC-regulated vehicles.
evidence: 3 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (243% increase)
Z-score of 6.43 indicates statistically significant cluster
Complements traffic spike (409% up) and illegal parking baseline (1,961 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Contact TLC and NYPD to determine nature of complaints (illegal pickups, unsafe driving, blocking traffic)
Interview drivers and residents about driver behavior changes; investigate whether surge correlates with surge pricing or increased demand

themes_detail.label: Water System Failures Escalate
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints surged to 33 three weeks ago vs. 10.5 weekly average (214% increase, z-score 4.39), coinciding with 460 water leak complaints and 609 plumbing complaints over 90 days—suggesting aging infrastructure.
evidence: 33 water system complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 10.5 weekly baseline (214% spike, z-score 4.39)
460 water leak complaints and 609 plumbing complaints over 90 days indicate chronic infrastructure stress
3,782 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days may reflect related building-system failures
reporting_angles: Request DEP data on main breaks and water pressure issues in Flatbush/PLG; investigate age and condition of water mains
Interview residents with recurring water/plumbing issues; analyze whether complaints cluster in specific neighborhoods (older housing stock vs. newer)

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog & Animal Safety Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% increase, z-score 6.35), suggesting either a breakdown in enforcement or new community safety concern around off-leash animals.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1,100% increase)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No sustained pattern in prior baseline suggests acute, recent trigger rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD Animal Care and Control about enforcement operations in district during spike period; verify if specific incidents triggered complaints
Talk to residents, dog owners, and park-goers about changes in off-leash dog prevalence and any recent injuries or confrontations
